newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary says plans 1996 spending cuts.
newsitem.headline: Hungary says plans 1996 spending cuts.

text.p: Hungary's Finance Ministry said on Monday it plans to slash state budget expenditures by more than 10 billion forints at the end of this year in anticipation of a wider-than-expected social security deficit.

The cuts are expected to help the country keep its budget deficit below four percent of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) as agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in March, when the IMF granted a stand-by loan to Hungary.

The total deficit of the two social security funds - health and pension - is likely to grow to 58 billion forints this year, Tibor Draskovics, State Secretary of the Finance Ministry was quoted as saying by the Hungarian news agency MTI.
The social security deficit target for 1996 was 17.8 billion forints, but earlier this year analysts and the National Bank of Hungary said the deficit may soar to around 70 billion forints.
The Finance Ministry said earlier that Hungary would plug the larger-than-planned gap of the social security budget with surplus revenues of the central state budget.

Draskovics, however, acknowledged that the surplus revenues will not completely cover the social security deficit, and Hungary will have to freeze some 10 to 12 billion forints which would otherwise be paid to government agencies.

The Finance Ministry also plans to freeze certain expenditures of the social security funds, he said. There were no further details and Draskovics noted that the planned cuts have not yet been approved. They are likely to be put to the cabinet at its next meeting on Thursday.
Hungary's GDP is expected to reach 6,610 billion forints this year.
